name: GJ 1245 B
description: A star 0.14 solar radii and 0.12 solar masses that turns once in 17 hours; its magnetic field has been mapped.

radius.source: Morin et al., arXiv:1005.5552, Table 1: radius 0.14 solar radii (theoretical radius)

mass.source: Morin et al., arXiv:1005.5552, Table 1: mass 0.12 solar masses

temperature.source: TESS Input Catalog 8.2 (VizieR IV/39/tic82), TIC 274127413: Teff

spin.source: Morin et al., arXiv:1005.5552, Table 1: rotation period 0.71 d and an axis 40 degrees from the line of sight, the values its magnetic maps were made with

color.reason: The Washington Double Star catalogue (Mason et al. 2001, AJ 122, 3466; VizieR B/wds/wds) lists WDS 19539+4425 GIC 159 AB: 6 arcsec apart, magnitudes 14.26 and 14.96: the companion gives 34.4% of the light, which a measured spectrum would blend with the star's. The color is the Planck spectrum at the star's temperature

text.card: A star 14% of the Sun's width that turns once in 17 hours, with a mapped magnetic field.
text.introduction: Morin et al. give it 0.14 solar radii, 0.12 solar masses, a rotation period of 17 hours and an axis tilted 40° from the line of sight.
